Residual_RH and Residual_v10m are positively correlated (Pearson 0.38, Spearman 0.35). The data doesn't settle the direction. Regressing each on the other with polynomial terms gave almost the same fit both ways (R² about 0.150 versus 0.153), and the residual checks I ran didn't favour either direction.

I chose B on physical grounds. Meridional wind advects air masses, so a change in v10m brings in moister or drier air and shifts relative humidity. Relative humidity has no comparable direct effect on the 10 m wind. This is a judgement from atmospheric physics, not something the data demonstrates.

ANSWER: B
